pr_title: Fix import hints that are followed by dot.number
pr_body:
Fixes #78881.

pr_comments:
Could you please also update the docs: `String.validate_node_name()`, `StringName.validate_node_name()`?

> Returns a copy of the string with all characters that are not allowed in Node.name removed (. : @ / " %).

```gdscript
# 4.0.3: 123
# master: 1_2_3
print("1.2@3".validate_node_name())
```

This is not directly related to the PR title, but it is also a consequence of #75760.

So I did some testing, it seems like it's a decent workaround for the current regression, though this warrants further work to make things more robust.

The key change here is that this logic used to run _before_ validating the node names, so we could properly handle the `.001` from Blender. Now that it runs after the rename, we can't differentiate between `.001` and `_001` coming from Blender. So e.g. in 4.0.3, a node named `Cube-convcolonly_001` would not be handled as having the `-convcolonly` hint, while with this change it will.

Also worth noting that the current code is super hacky and greedy, and will replace random sequences of `.`, `_` and numbers at the end of any hint. So `mycube123-col0128_9128.1789.198.22` would become `mycube123`. This really needs to be cleaned up in the future.

To test this I made this scene derived from the MRP of #78881:

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/58742944-9536-403d-81a2-008124794cae)

Test project with blend and exported glb and dae:
[ImportHints.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/11958327/ImportHints.zip)

### 4.0.3

Here's how it imports in 4.0.3 using different formats (.blend file directly, .glb exported from Blender 3.6, .dae exported from Blender 3.6):

#### blend

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/f6637af0-88a9-4142-a989-f1fb907cb187)

Behaves as expected for the 4.0.3 logic, the `.001` and `.002` hints are properly handled. The one I added with `_002` which is invalid syntax for an import hint is left untouched, so it's imported as a normal cube and keeps its name.

The `Cube-convcolonly` which conflicts with the existing `Cube` gets auto-renamed to solve the naming conflict.

#### glb

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/53cc88be-282a-422f-b623-adc0df2cbb26)

Similar behavior as blend, minus the light and camera but that's properly from not setting the right export settings, and unrelated to this issue.

#### dae

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/363d131b-36f8-45e9-92d3-46bda794bd85)

Also similar result. The scene tree order seems backwards, but that might be a bug in the Collada pipeline which we don't actively maintain.

### 4.1 RC 3

Reproducing the bug first to be able to validate the change.

#### blend

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/5da2937e-b064-4bfe-86f1-f5f3b1e3214d)

As expected, hints aren't properly handled, aside from the one on `Cube-convcolonly`.

Worth noting that the node name disambiguation logic changed too, so it's no longer named `@Cube@...` but it's actually using the node type instead with `@StaticBody3D@...`. This may or may not be another intentional change from #75760 (judging by the code I would say it's intentional and part of the optimization).

#### glb

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/76d162d2-b204-4e3f-8c90-df392800b21a)

Consistent with blend.

#### dae

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/5dbbc576-dbe7-4697-ae11-8cd769d4600b)

Consistent with above results too. Note how the name conflict handling differs between the glTF and collada pipelines (duplicate `Cube-convcolonly_002` becomes respectively `Cube-convcolonly_0022` for glTF and `Cube-convcolonly_003` for collada).

### This PR

Confirming that it fixes the issue on the "expected" case of having `.001` suffix, and creates a minor bug with now supporting `_001` as a valid suffix to trim too. This is a slight breakage, but I think acceptable to fix the regression in the short term.

#### blend

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/556027b3-451e-4043-b099-40b613965575)

As expected, fixes the bug, creates a minor behavior change for `Cube-convcolonly_002` which is now handled as a `-convcolonly` hint. Technically a bug, could be considered a feature ;)

#### glb

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/a0c69cf7-af34-4558-ad89-c1bf7949d970)

Same result.

#### dae

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/2082a7cc-db2d-400b-9b26-e3d145b6a51e)

Also working as expected.

---

**TL;DR:** It's not perfect, but I think it's good enough to YOLO merge now for 4.1 and fix the regression. I'd appreciate that the @godotengine/import teams looks further into it afterwards anyway, and makes sure that this system is more robust.
@capnm Could you rebase your branch? The current version is 800+ commits behind `master`, would be good to reduce the diff.

issue_context.title: Import Hints are no Longer Processed if the Object Name ends with a Number
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.1 rc2

### System information

Manjaro GL-Compatibility

### Issue description

When using import hints, such as -col or -colonly, on object names Godot used to accept the hint even if it was followed by Blender's auto duplicate naming scheme such as .001 or .002. This is no longer the case, items name to the likes of "object-col.001" will not import with collision.

I noticed that, prior to 4.1, Godot would remove periods from imported object names. Object.001 would import as Object001, but now it would import as Object_001. Perhaps this change broke the import hint behavior.

### Steps to reproduce

Export a scene with object names using import hints, such as -col or -convcol, where some of the objects have '.001' or similar appended to the end of their names. Import the scene into Godot and create an inherited scene.

### Minimal reproduction project

[ImportHints.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/11919131/ImportHints.zip)
comments:
I can confirm this on 4.1.dev1-4.1.rc1 and 4.1.rc 46424488e using https://github.com/godotengine/tps-demo. This does not occur on 4.0.3.stable.

I bisected the regression to 223ce4fcb958619d0f3c62e79a2b5846240e7ff3. cc @reduz

> I bisected the regression to [223ce4f](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/223ce4fcb958619d0f3c62e79a2b5846240e7ff3). cc @reduz

As pointed out in the OP, this commit made it so that `.` in node names gets replaced by `_` instead of simply removed.

So the logic here needs to be changed to take this into account:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/cdd2313ba27d0a2600a18e849b4c5d1fd6a6e351/editor/import/resource_importer_scene.cpp#L313-L353

@godotengine/import
I'm not able to rush fix this for a RC build. How to proceed?
I think this will have to be a known issue in 4.1 and we'll fix it in 4.1.1.

review_comments:
GH won't let you comment on the right line but: The comment should be amended to clarify, it's talking about `.number` and we're handling `_number`.

I'm also a bit surprised that the fix is this, reduz's PR changed it to replace `.` by `_` instead of an empty string. But here it sounds like the previous logic still handled `.` so it happened _before_ the replacement, and now it seems to happen after?
I think he did it right :) I can just replace the old `hint.num3er` with `hint_num3er`.
